top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) rests on demonstrated results: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the trap light shift while many neutral atoms are interrogated in parallel, and independent groups reproduce 1e-18-level accuracy and stability. That is distinct in kind from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, the two-name allocation needs no arbitrary exclusion, and the citation can be kept narrow to magic-wavelength lattice trapping. P002 is a strong rival on conceptual reach but forces the Mele versus Hasan and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang exclusion; P003 is real science but the pairing mechanism is open and the trio omits first authors; no award is worse than any of the three mature candidates.
recusal_note: Doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Hall is associated with the frequency-comb work on which the Ye group builds. No documented collaboration with Katori or Ye, and my atomic-physics background biases me toward precision measurement. Possible recusal question on P001, but I do not think it is required.
